blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — The 72-year-old journalist recently sued for cyberlibel by the husband of Vice President Sara Duterte will ask that the case be transferred to Metro Manila instead of being tried in Davao City, where the complaint was filed, citing fears for his safety. But still, Philip Lustre Jr. on Wednesday said the charges filed by lawyer Manases “Mans” Carpio would not stop his current book project on the Vice President, which he said would include her ongoing Senate impeachment trial. “As my friends said in jest, [the case] is promoting my books,” said Lustre, who earlier authored “Kill, Kill, […]...
